title: Midsegments, Bisectors, and Triangle Centers
seo_title: Midsegment, Centroid and Triangle Centers Worksheet (Geometry) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on midsegments, perpendicular and angle bisectors, the centroid, circumcenter, incenter and the Triangle Inequality. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A midsegment is half the third side. The centroid splits each median 2 : 1.
key_sub: Any two sides of a triangle add to more than the third side.
body_html:
How it works

Midsegment Theorem: a segment joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side and half as long.

A point on a perpendicular bisector is the same distance from the segment's endpoints. A point on an angle bisector is the same distance from the angle's sides.

  • Circumcenter: perpendicular bisectors meet; same distance from the vertices.
  • Incenter: angle bisectors meet; same distance from the sides.
  • Centroid: medians meet; it is 2/3 of the way along each median from the vertex (AG = 2 × GM).
  • Orthocenter: altitudes meet.

Triangle Inequality: any two sides add to more than the third. The longest side is opposite the largest angle.

Example

D and E are midpoints of two sides. DE = 3x + 1 and the third side is 8x − 6. Find DE.

2(3x + 1) = 8x − 6

6x + 2 = 8x − 6, so x = 4

Answer: DE = 13

Example

Two sides of a triangle are 7 and 12. What lengths can the third side have?

Bigger than 12 − 7 = 5

Smaller than 12 + 7 = 19

Answer: 5 < x < 19

Common mistakes

  • Doubling the midsegment when you should halve it. The midsegment is the short one.
  • Splitting a median in half at the centroid. The ratio is 2 : 1, with the long part at the vertex.
  • Mixing up circumcenter (vertices) and incenter (sides).
  • Accepting 3, 4, 7 as a triangle. 3 + 4 = 7 is not more than 7.

faq.q: What is the Triangle Midsegment Theorem?
faq.a: The segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half its length.

faq.q: What is the difference between the circumcenter and the incenter?
faq.a: The circumcenter is where the perpendicular bisectors meet and is equidistant from the vertices. The incenter is where the angle bisectors meet and is equidistant from the sides.

faq.q: How far is the centroid along a median?
faq.a: Two thirds of the way from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, so it splits the median in a 2 : 1 ratio.

faq.q: What is the Triangle Inequality Theorem?
faq.a: The sum of any two side lengths of a triangle is greater than the third side length.

items.q: The sides of a triangle are 36, 12 and 46. The three midsegments form a smaller triangle. What is its perimeter?
items.e: Each midsegment is half of a side, so the perimeter is half: (36 + 12 + 46) ÷ 2 = 47.

items.q: D and E are midpoints. DE = 5x + 5 and AB = 8x + 18. Find AB.
Point D is on the perpendicular bisector of EF. DE = 7x + 13 and DF = 6x + 19. Find DE.
items.e: Perpendicular Bisector Theorem: a point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the endpoints, so DE = DF. 7x + 13 = 6x + 19, so x = 6. The length is 55.

items.q: Point M is on the bisector of ∠JKL. Its distances to the two sides of the angle are 5x − 5 and 4x − 3. Find the distance.
items.e: Angle Bisector Theorem: a point on an angle bisector is equidistant from the two sides of the angle. 5x − 5 = 4x − 3, so x = 2. The length is 5.

items.q: Point P is on the perpendicular bisector of AB. PA = 3x + 1 and PB = 7x − 19. Find PA.
items.e: Perpendicular Bisector Theorem: a point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the endpoints, so PA = PB. 3x + 1 = 7x − 19, so 4x = 20 and x = 5. The length is 16.

items.q: Point D is on the bisector of ∠XYZ. Its distances to the two sides of the angle are 3x + 14 and 4x + 8. Find x.

items.q: G is the centroid of △ABC and AG = 18. Find the length of the median AM.
items.e: AG is 2/3 of AM, so GM = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 and AM = 18 + 9 = 27.

items.q: G is the centroid of △ABC and AG = 16. Find GM.
items.e: GM is half of AG: 16 ÷ 2 = 8.

items.q: G is the centroid of △ABC and AG = 30. Find GM.

items.q: G is the centroid of △ABC. AG = 2x + 24 and GM = 2x + 7. Find x.
items.e: The centroid is twice as far from the vertex as from the midpoint: AG = 2 × GM. 2x + 24 = 2(2x + 7), so x = 5.

items.q: G is the centroid of △ABC. AG = x + 1 and GM = x − 4. Find x.

items.q: G is the centroid of △ABC and GM = 2. Find AG.
items.e: Centroid Theorem: AG is 2/3 of the median and GM is 1/3, so AG = 2 × GM = 4.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the balance point of the triangle?
items.e: The centroid is the balance point of the triangle.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is where the lines through each vertex perpendicular to the opposite side meet?
items.e: The orthocenter is where the lines through each vertex perpendicular to the opposite side meet.

items.q: The angle bisectors of a triangle meet at which point?
items.e: The angle bisectors meet at the incenter.

items.q: The medians of a triangle meet at which point?
items.e: The medians meet at the centroid.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the same distance from all three vertices?
items.e: The circumcenter is the same distance from all three vertices.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the center of a circle that touches all three sides?
items.e: The incenter is the center of a circle that touches all three sides.

items.q: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle meet at which point?
items.e: The perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet at the circumcenter.

items.q: Where is the orthocenter of a right triangle?
c: At the vertex of the right angle
At the midpoint of the hypotenuse
items.e: The two legs are altitudes, and they meet at the right angle. At the vertex of the right angle.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is 2/3 of the way from each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side?
items.e: The centroid is 2/3 of the way from each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

items.q: Three friends live at different houses and want to meet at a point equally far from all three. Which center?
items.e: The circumcenter is the same distance from the three vertices (points). Circumcenter.

items.q: Which center is always inside the triangle?
items.e: Angle bisectors and medians stay inside every triangle. The incenter (and the centroid).

items.q: In an equilateral triangle, how are the four centers placed?
c: Two are inside and two are outside
They are all the same point
items.e: Every bisector, median and altitude is the same line in an equilateral triangle. They are all the same point.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the same distance from all three sides?
items.e: The incenter is the same distance from all three sides.

items.q: A park ranger wants a lookout the same distance from three straight roads that form a triangle. Which center?
items.e: The incenter is the same distance from the three sides (lines). Incenter.

items.q: Where is the circumcenter of an obtuse triangle?
items.e: The perpendicular bisectors meet outside, beyond the longest side. Outside the triangle.

items.q: A student wants to balance a triangular piece of cardboard on a pencil tip. Which center?
items.e: The centroid is the balance point. Centroid.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is where the heights meet?
items.e: The orthocenter is where the heights meet.

items.q: Where is the circumcenter of a right triangle?
c: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse
items.e: The hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle through the three vertices. At the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

items.q: Which point of a triangle is the center of a circle through all three vertices?
items.e: The circumcenter is the center of a circle through all three vertices.

items.q: The altitudes of a triangle meet at which point?
items.e: The altitudes meet at the orthocenter.

items.q: Can 8, 9 and 17 be the side lengths of a triangle?
c: Only if two sides are equal
Only if it is a right triangle
items.e: Triangle Inequality: the two shorter sides must add to more than the longest. 8 + 9 = 17, which is equal to 17. No. (Equal sums make a flat line, not a triangle.)

items.q: Two sides of a triangle are 12 and 19. Which describes the possible lengths x of the third side?
items.e: The third side is longer than the difference and shorter than the sum: 19 − 12 < x < 12 + 19. 7 < x < 31.
